newsitem.title: USA: West Virginia plans to appeal tobacco lawsuit dismissal.
newsitem.headline: West Virginia plans to appeal tobacco lawsuit dismissal.

text.p: The West Virginia attorney general's office said Tuesday it plans to appeal last week's dismissal of most of its lawsuit against tobacco companies, which seeks to recover public health costs of smoking-related illnesses.
"It's our intent (to appeal)," said Deborah McHenry, deputy managing attorney general. "It's our opinion that the decision of the circuit court judge was wrong based on both fact and law."

Kanawha County Circuit Judge Irene Berger on Thursday dismissed all of the state's claims for fraud, negligence, unjust enrichment and conspiracy. She ruled the attorney general's office lacked authority from the state legislature to pursue the claim.
Berger let stand allegations that the tobacco industry's manufacturing and marketing of cigarettes violated state consumer protection and antitrust statutes.
A hearing to determine whether the attorney general can proceed with those claims is set for Thursday in Berger's court.

West Virginia's lawsuit was originally filed in September 1994 against 17 tobacco companies and sought unspecified damages. At least 20 other states have filed lawsuits against tobacco companies seeking to recover public health costs of treating smoking-related illnesses.
McHenry said smoking-related illnesses kill about 4,000 West Virginia residents each year and that treating sick smokers costs the state in excess of $100 million annually.
